items.title: Continuous OA mark
items.question: Does this mark represent Operations Automated strongly enough to become the controlled master direction?
items.description: The continuous O-to-A loop expresses connection, movement and an operation becoming more capable.

items.title: Signature colour and atmosphere
items.question: Does the Obsidian, deep-blue and electric-cyan direction feel capable, modern and human enough?
items.description: Dark signature surfaces create recognition; light working surfaces protect readability and approachability.

items.title: Typography
items.question: Does geometric display type with a clear sans-serif body match how Operations Automated should communicate?
items.description: Strong display type carries the identity. Source Sans and its fallbacks carry working content.

items.title: Connected background language
items.question: Does the restrained mesh and connection field add meaning without becoming decorative technology imagery?
items.description: Connection fields should imply relationships and flow, never fictional circuitry or AI magic.

items.title: Workbench application pilot
items.question: Does the brand remain practical when applied to a real working application?
items.description: The Workbench is the first bounded application adoption. It uses the shared tokens and controlled OA mark.

items.title: Documentation direction
items.question: Does the lighter document treatment still feel unmistakably part of Operations Automated?
items.description: Controlled documents prioritise reading, evidence and status while retaining the brand hierarchy.

items.title: LinkedIn profile cover
items.question: Is the supplied personal-profile cover the right public-facing composition, subject to wording approval?
items.description: The 1584 × 396 cover keeps the lower-left area comparatively quiet for LinkedIn's profile-photo overlay.

items.title: Descriptor and strapline
items.question: Should the source wording be retained, revised or rejected before any public use?
items.description: Operations consultancy may narrow the company. Autonomise may imply autonomy as a default rather than a governed option.

boundary: An item-level review is retained as evidence. It does not change artefact status, merge the pull request or authorise external publication.
